chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I read in the letter of a man to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The two Rak'at which are before the Fajr prayer, are they from the night prayer or from the daytime prayer, and at what time should I pray them?' So he wrote in his own handwriting: 'Include them in the night prayer completely.'
ai.seo_question: Are the two Rak'at before Fajr considered part of the night prayer or daytime prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential classification of the two Rak'at before Fajr, ruling that they are 'inserted' (hashwan) into the night prayer rather than the day prayer. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view that the pre-dawn Sunnah retains the temporal and spiritual characteristics of the night, emphasizing the continuity of worship from the night hours into the dawn. The term 'hashwan' implies a flexible integration, allowing these units to be counted within the broader scope of Salat al-Layl while still being performed at the specific time of Fajr.
